verdicts.identification: Xweardes rig8 Metin2 game-bot login, updater and DLL injector
evidence: Ghidra FUN_14000fad0 only calls injector FUN_140005a30 after selecting a game process and clicking Inject; process enumeration filters metin2client. Injector checks WOW64, writes the selected local DLL path, starts LoadLibraryW remotely, waits and checks completion.

FUN_140006240 derives the local rig8.lic path. FUN_140006f90 reads that file and uses CryptUnprotectData. Remember me saves the entered license with CryptProtectData. No browser-store collection was found.

FUN_140009d30 uses HTTPS to api.xweardes.com/rig8. Login submits key plus ephemeral public key; session requests submit the obtained token. The updater verifies an ECDSA P-256 manifest signature and SHA-256 file digests before replacement; restart executes its own updated image.

Recovered current manifest, site and site JavaScript with forager. Website advertises Metin2 Bot and its game scripting API. The manifest names qwy.dll and d3dx9_43.dll; both were recovered with manifest SHA-256 verification and provenance.

Recovered qwy.dll DllMain FUN_10110740 checks/patches in-game anti-cheat module CB.cbm, hooks loader APIs and game networking, and starts game/overlay threads. Session helper reads Local\xw8c-5f3a91d2, validates a live loader PID and performs ECDH authentication. Winsock hook FUN_100db820 filters CB traffic and otherwise forwards the original game connect call. No evidence of unrelated host credential collection or off-host secret export was found.

IsDebuggerPresent and TerminateProcess callers resolve to MSVC runtime/error handling; keyboard/clipboard APIs serve the ImGui user interface. The SHA-matched recovered DLL contains game-related memory modification and anti-cheat bypass, which are consistent with the advertised cheat purpose.

Recovered d3dx9_43.dll identifies Direct3D 9 Extensions 9.29.952.3111 and reports verified Microsoft Corporation signature provenance; exports provide the expected D3DX support. This distinguishes the game dependency from a name-only DLL claim.
verdicts.context_missing: Whether a user intentionally installed this cheat and the game operator allows it is unknown. BENIGN here identifies the observed game tool behavior, not an endorsement of cheating or remote update trust.
verdicts.source_label_explanation: Administrator request, debug privilege, remote memory writes, remote threads, downloaded DLLs and game anti-cheat bypass can explain the high sandbox score without establishing general-purpose malware.

verdicts.identification: passport-platform 0.1.0 licensing and telemetry package with environment leak
evidence: Read all 22 archive members. Core import only exports helpers; no install hook or immediate import-time network activity. Explicit enforceLicense invokes sendHeartbeat; NestJS bootstrap calls enforceLicense unless JEST_WORKER_ID is set.

dist/heartbeat.js serializes product/domain/version/status AND envs: process.env into the same fetch POST body. It uses the real process.env even when the consuming app supplies a restricted getEnv function. Errors are swallowed and timeout defaults to 2 seconds.

README API table promises only product/domain/version/status/at and describes a small telemetry heartbeat. Sending all environment variables is an undisclosed secret-bearing expansion unrelated to token verification.

Token verification locally checks a signed base64url payload and public key; domain and expiry govern exit. No hardcoded collection endpoint, downloaded code, filesystem harvesting, or arbitrary command execution was found. Endpoint comes from the consuming application.
verdicts.context_missing: Runtime endpoint, environment contents and actual receipt are unknown. The static body construction proves the export path without assuming runtime success. An explicitly authorized diagnostic deployment could change intent, but no such context is present.
verdicts.coverage_gap: One distinct suspicious objective is justified: full-environment HTTP export. Licensing failure, Jest skipping, public-key verification, normal environment reads and timer use do not justify inventing a second hostile behavior.

evidence: Decoded scripts.postinstall creates a temporary directory, builds a package manifest named with an OpenSSL random-hex suffix and fixed description foobar, then constructs npm publish <tempdir> from np / m pu / blish fragments through printf command substitution. It finally removes the temp directory.

npm publish would use the installing user or CI runner registry configuration. The package does not explicitly read or transmit the npm token, and its generated description contains no victim data in this version. This is unauthorized use/testing of publication authority, rather than evidence of token theft or worm propagation.
index.js only logs the same search link as README. Naming and documentation identify a proof of concept, but there is no opt-in guard on the postinstall publish attempt.
verdicts.context_missing: A controlled researcher installation and actual publication success are unknown. The default automatic, concealed publishing action tips the verdict despite the proof-of-concept name.

rule_corrections: Retained parsed form-named member reads; moved generic member text from browser UI to source member syntax. Renamed the generic value-reference union and retained its credential-field consumer.

Moved license-function names from privilege to source naming, retaining Apps Script exclusion membership. Renamed the Clipboard token as a neutral name reference; kept its matcher and .NET composite requirements.
Renamed CNG import/sign composites to API profiles. Co-occurrence does not establish call order or reuse of the same key; predicates and passkey consumer membership are retained.

Moved postinstall temp utility/package-manifest reference to notable neutral temporary-directory capability. Temp-only fixture proves the unsupported credential-theft implication. Added distinct suspicious runtime command assembly and install-time generated package publishing coverage, plus notable npm publish and OpenSSL random-hex command observations.

Replaced ineffective full-call regex for environment fetch bodies with structural direct/nested JSON body alternatives. Moved the neutral source-to-body observation to HTTP request/body. The POST consumer is suspicious because the required evidence alone does not prove unauthorized transfer. Actual passport bytes independently establish deceptive environment export.

Renamed the JSON.stringify env-token observation to describe its actual scope: it matches env keys, env-named values and process.env members. Preserved its original matcher and Boolean/presence-probe exclusions, and updated the GitHub Action consumer and positive/negative expectations. Both the benign environment-value control and the known hostile post-step fixture retain coverage.

Audited saturated directories and found no exact duplicate conditions. Moved quoted Run string-table syntax from property access to source literals, and upload/backup/exfil object-key syntax from HTTP bodies to source key-value syntax. Preserved matcher/defaults, all explicit consumers and positive/negative controls; audited 23 HTTP ancestor-selector contexts. These source tokens do not independently establish property access or HTTP traffic. No directory budget was increased.

Grouped Tree-sitter predicates with the direct/nested structural alternatives; unrelated function and serializer near misses do not match. Removed unreachable Text scope from two AST-dependent AI-prompt consumers. No previously firing sample detection depended on those dead type combinations.

verification.component_checks: Four direct evaluator checks pass; ordinary reports omit unmatched component observations.
verification.retained_positive: Existing malicious gha-larkspurguard-post-step-exfil-linux.tgz still emits hostile gha-post-step-repository-exfil; env-value-stringify-controls.js retains environment serialization observation.

material_detection_losses: None on the three samples after explicit ID relocation mapping. All accurate observations remain; misleading descriptions and placements were corrected. Temp-package reference remains at notable, while distinct concealed execution and automatic publication are suspicious. The generic full-environment POST rule is suspicious because authorization is absent from its required evidence.
classifier_disagreement: Terminal Atomscan verdict remains BENIGN for both malicious npm packages despite probability increases and new suspicious findings. JSON calibrated levels stay -1. This is a classifier/calibration gap; no duplicate or unsupported traits were added to force its verdict. Atomscan reports loading model spec v18 while the extractor expects v19; newer features are zero-filled. This compatibility warning is a material limitation of the classifier comparison.
